title: Controllable Traffic Simulation through LLM-Guided Hierarchical Reasoning and Refinement

control_signal.value: Natural-language description of the desired scenario (for example a cut-in event) given by the user, alongside road topology and agent states.

control_mechanism.value: An LLM (GPT-4o) uses chain-of-thought to write a Frenet-frame cost function; its gradient guides diffusion sampling at test time, and a refinement module revises the cost from failed trajectory coordinates.

base_model.value: Transformer-based diffusion model following EDM, with map, agent-map and agent-agent attention and relative coordinates; 32 sampling steps; 3 attention layers, 24 agents, 200 lane polylines.

datasets.value: Waymo Open Motion Dataset: trained on the 69,500-scenario training split, evaluated on 1,000 validation scenarios.

metrics.value: ADE, FDE, JSD, collision and offroad rate (conditional); scene collision rate, MMD (unconditional); cost-function correctness and guidance success rate across four event types (guided).

controllability_evidence.value: Guidance success rate over four event types, 20 scenarios each, beat a target-point baseline and improved with refinement (Table IV); exact values not in packet. Unconditional SCR 6.3% vs 9.7% and 11.2%.

stated_limitations.value: The refinement module struggles to fix cost functions when the LLM's initial understanding of the scenario is fundamentally wrong.

notes: Table IV success-rate numbers are missing from the packet. Conditional-simulation JSD is slightly worse than state of the art (page 5).
